explain.say: A frog and a lizard both sit in the sun, both have four legs, and both lay eggs. So are they the same kind of animal? Let's put them side by side and look for the clues, like a detective.

faq.a: No. A frog is an amphibian. It has smooth, damp skin, lays jelly eggs in water, and its young are tadpoles that live in water.
An amphibian is an animal that usually starts life in water breathing with gills, then lives on land with lungs as an adult. Frogs, toads, newts and salamanders are amphibians.

faq.q: What makes an animal a reptile?
faq.a: Reptiles have dry, scaly skin, breathe only with lungs, and most lay tough-shelled eggs on land. Snakes, lizards, turtles and crocodiles are reptiles.
A frog takes in some of its air through its thin skin, and that only works when the skin is damp. Frogs also drink water through their skin.
asks: Do frogs breathe through their skin?

faq.a: No. Baby reptiles hatch from eggs looking like small adults. Only amphibians have a tadpole or larva stage in water.
asks: Do baby lizards live in water?

facts: Frogs absorb oxygen and water through their thin, moist skin.
The wood frog can survive having much of its body water frozen in winter.
